correctness.rationale: Reviewed the actual seven-blob Git package and independently recomputed its exact Git tree identity. The stated domain is odd primes p, R=Z/p^2, primitive free determinant-zero rank-one matrix submodules, complete affine cosets and unnormalized counting norms. Every ray is indexed uniquely by two projective points; each projective point has p^2+p two-chart representatives. A character at xi is an eigenvector of T*T with eigenvalue p^2 times the ray count L(xi). Smith normal form gives exactly six strata; chart orthogonality gives multipliers L= p^2(p+1)^2, p^2(2p+1), p^2(p+1), p(p+1), 2p^2, 3p^2. Rank-one residue matrices number N1=(p-1)(p+1)^2, invertible residue matrices N2=(p^2-1)(p^2-p); determinant-one-linear-congruence lifting gives p^3 versus p^4-p^3 primitive rank-one lifts and the table totals p^8. All L are positive. Constant and nonconstant extrema yield kappa_all^2=p(p+1) and kappa_meanzero^2=p(2p+1)/(p+1), with p=3 as the smallest admitted prime (p=2 would have coincident levels). GL_2(R)xGL_2(R) transitivity on ray views preserves character input subspaces; convex averaging over permutations establishes uniform weighting as a minimizer even allowing zero weights (singular weights have infinite condition number). Independently reconstructed prior determinant-cone Fourier transform and primitive-ray Ramanujan bridge, symbolically verified all six entries for arbitrary indeterminate p; separately exhaustively counted 256 frequencies at p=2 (out-of-domain boundary) and all 6561 at p=3, plus six representative frequencies at p=5. No code logs alone are used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: A previously public full theorem, Universal Fourier spectrum of the determinant-zero cone over finite chain rings (Resultary record dated 2026-11-01; public Git commit 2026-11-08T20:01:35Z), supplies the complete additive Fourier transform of C={X:det X=0} for every finite chain ring. The present R=Z/p^2 theorem is obtained from its k=2 case by the elementary decomposition C=P disjoint union pM_2(R), with P the primitive determinant-zero matrices, and the ring Ramanujan-sum identity. For each dual frequency xi, C-hat(xi)=p^2 L(xi)-p K(xi)+p^4 1_{xi in pM_2(R)}, where L counts orthogonal primitive null rays and K counts rays orthogonal modulo p. K=p^2(p+1)^2 if xi is divisible by p, p^2(2p+1) for primitive rank-one reductions, and p^2(p+1) for primitive rank-two reductions. Substitution of the previously established cone multipliers yields all six submitted L values exactly: p^2(p+1)^2, p^2(2p+1), p^2(p+1), p(p+1), 2p^2, and 3p^2. The residue-rank and determinant-lift multiplicities are the same standard Smith strata used in the cone theorem. The remaining scalar-view optimality is a group-symmetrization lemma: GL_2(R)xGL_2(R) is transitive on primitive rank-one ray directions, and averaging a weight vector does not raise the maximum or lower the minimum over Fourier modes, including when the constant mode is omitted. An earlier published null-ray finite-field theorem explicitly employs this group-averaging principle. Thus both spectral classification and minimax weighting are logically covered by a stronger earlier result together with routine consequences. The reviewed source was first committed at 2026-11-08T20:29:40Z, after the covering cone theorem was publicly committed at 20:01:35Z. The latter alone does not print the exact six-row null-ray table, but the implication is exact, not a title match.

value.rationale: The determinant-null ray family and sharp inverse stability are naturally motivated; an exact six-level singular spectrum can in principle be valuable. In this instance, however, every exact ray frequency multiplier, its multiplicity and the two conditioning endpoints are routine algebraic consequences of the already public arbitrary-chain-ring determinant-cone Fourier formula by the elementary Ramanujan bridge C=P ⊔ pM_2(R). Uniform scalar view-weight optimality is a generic transitive-group averaging consequence explicitly used by previous finite-field null-ray tomography. Consequently the final package contains no independently unknown natural exact invariant or nonroutine structural result after proper recognition of coverage. The result remains a correct illustrative specialization, not a distinct contribution.
